messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@brightcart.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Support model and SLA for upcoming pilot

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We want to lock the commercial guardrails before the engineering ramp next month. A quick summary of BrightCart's ask for the pilot:

- Pilot scope: inference for checkout recommendations, expected steady-state 50 rps, peak up to 500 rps during promos.
- Uptime target: looking for 99.95% availability SLA for the inference endpoint and multi-zone failover.
- Response velocity: P1 acknowledgement within 1 hour, P1 remediation escalation path needed.
- On-call / retainer: interested in a technical retainer for priority triage during our promotional windows (Nov–Dec cadence).
- Credits/penalties: want a clear formula for credits if SLA misses occur; also want assurance around a limited number of 'stability incidents' for the pilot period where we won't be penalized heavily.

Can you share a sketch of package options and an initial ballpark for any retainer + associated discounts for a >3 month pilot that could convert to an annual commit? Procurement may ask for a worked example of how credits would be applied.

Attaching our internal availability expectation doc (sent separately).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightCart
procurement@brightcart.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2026-12-11T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Support model and SLA for upcoming pilot

Elena —

Great notes, thanks. Below is a concise offering tailored to the pilot and the conversion path to a 12-month commit. I’ve included a worksheet (SLA_Worksheet_BrightCart.xlsx) that models crediting and cost impact.

High-level options (pilot -> conversion guidance):

1) Operational Standard (pilot-friendly)
- Uptime target: 99.9%
- Response: P1 acknowledge within 2 hours, escalation to engineering on-call within 6 hours
- Retainer: optional (recommended during promo windows)
- Stability credits: 2% of monthly invoice per P1 incident (capped at 10% in pilot month)
- Ideal for: teams wanting lower up-front retainer cost and standard routing

2) Assured (recommended for BrightCart)
- Uptime target: 99.95% (multi-zone)
- Response: P1 acknowledge within 1 hour; P1 on-call engagement within 1 hour; P2 within 4 hours
- Retainer: $9,500 / month (24/7 priority triage and 2 dedicated escalation seats during promo windows)
- Stability credits: 5% monthly credit for SLA miss; for pilot months we offer a one-time escalated credit allowance up to 20% for the first major incident while we finalize routing rules
- Conversion discount: 10% off committed usage if convert to a 12-month reserved capacity within 30 days of pilot close

3) Assured+ (enterprise escalation bundle)
- Uptime target: 99.97%
- Response: P1 engage within 30 minutes; designated named responder and monthly runbook reviews
- Retainer: $18,000 / month + guaranteed standby during promo peaks
- Stability credits: sliding scale starting at 5% and increasing by incident severity (worksheet models this)

Proposal notes and next steps:
- Pilot recommendation: Assured tier with the $9.5k retainer for the promo window and the 3-month pilot. That balances cost vs. risk for BrightCart's peak demand.
- Crediting: See SLA_Worksheet_BrightCart.xlsx — it shows sample invoices and how credits apply across months and a pro-rata approach for partial-month incidents.
- Procurement questions: we can produce a detailed crediting formula for legal if you want the exact clause language.

If this aligns, I’ll route an internal pricing check and provide a final term sheet. Are you available for a short call Wed 12/13 to run the worksheet together?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA_Worksheet_BrightCart.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Support model and SLA for upcoming pilot — pricing check

Laura / Marissa —

Quick read and recommendations:

1) Pilot allowance: OK to offer the one-time 20% capped stability credit for the first major incident, but add two constraints:
   - We require a signed runbook + production routing checklist (items listed in the SLA worksheet) before we enable the allowance.
   - Allowance only applies to the pilot months (first 90 days) and not after conversion.

2) Conversion discount: 10% is reasonable if they commit to a 12-month reserved throughput with predictable consumption bands. Add a true-up clause at quarterly intervals.

3) Retainer scope and operational guardrails:
   - $9,500 / month retainer covers up to 20 hours of named runbook/triage work per month and priority routing (beyond that billable at T&M).
   - Named escalation seats: up to 2 engineers with 24/7 paging; additional seats billed at $3k per seat / month.
   - For P1 escalations, on-call must respond within 1 hour; we offer up to 8 hours of on-site incident follow-through (remote) included in retainer per quarter.

4) Pricing impact: I ran a quick sensitivity in Pricing_impact_model.csv — with the 10% conversion discount plus the retainer we still have ~26% gross margin at expected pilot consumption. If they push for Assured+ we need a stronger commit.

If that looks good I’ll sign off on the term sheet language and legal can add the crediting formula.

Karthik
VP, Solutions Pricing
Attachments: Pricing_impact_model.csv

Thanks for the patience. Based on internal review we can confirm the following pilot commercial sketch and next steps:

Pilot commercial sketch (3 months):
- Tier: Assured
- Uptime: 99.95% (multi-zone)
- Retainer: $9,500 / month (covers priority triage, 2 named escalation seats, up to 20 runbook/troubleshooting hours / month)
- Stability credit: 5% monthly credit for SLA misses. For the pilot we will include a one-time allowance that can increase the credit up to 20% for the first qualifying major incident provided BrightCart completes the runbook and routing checklist before go-live.
- Conversion: 10% discount on committed usage if BrightCart signs a 12-month reserved capacity within 30 days of pilot close; quarterly true-up applies.
- Guardrails: allowance only during pilot months; after conversion standard crediting formula applies (see SLA_Worksheet_BrightCart.xlsx). Additional escalation seats or extended coverage billed per seat.

Next steps:
1) I’ll share a redlineable term sheet and the exact credit clause for legal review — expect DocuSign draft by EOD 12/15 (link included).
2) Please confirm acceptance of the retainer and pilot timeline; once confirmed we’ll schedule a runbook workshop with Solutions Engineering next week.
